rules.rationale: This macro equation expands bfBody into the exact MPY statement term for the submitted function, so it defines a named program term rather than adding an execution or mathematical fact.
This macro equation expands bfModule into the module containing the bf definition and therefore is a structural definition of a named proof term.
This macro equation expands bfCall into the ordinary MPY Call term with two string arguments, defining entry syntax without replacing call execution.
This equation defines planetValues as the fixed ordered eight-element planet sequence used by the mathematical postcondition.
This guarded equation is the Mercury case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 0 exactly when the input code sequence is Mercury.
This guarded equation is the Venus case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 1 exactly when the input code sequence is Venus.
This guarded equation is the Earth case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 2 exactly when the input code sequence is Earth.
This guarded equation is the Mars case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 3 exactly when the input code sequence is Mars.
This guarded equation is the Jupiter case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 4 exactly when the input code sequence is Jupiter.
This guarded equation is the Saturn case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 5 exactly when the input code sequence is Saturn.
This guarded equation is the Uranus case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 6 exactly when the input code sequence is Uranus.
This guarded equation is the Neptune case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 7 exactly when the input code sequence is Neptune.
This complementary guarded equation completes the planetIndex definition by assigning -1 exactly when the input differs from all eight planet names.
This equation defines betweenPlanets compositionally by applying the planetIndex definition to both inputs and passing the indices to betweenIndices.
This guarded equation defines the invalid-index case of betweenIndices as the empty value sequence whenever either index is negative.
This guarded equation defines the ascending-index case of betweenIndices as the slice strictly after I and before J.
This guarded equation defines the reverse-or-equal-index case of betweenIndices as the slice strictly after J and before I.
